answers: “I’ve been helping a relative of mine with a little allotment. I like having a practical job to get on with there. We keep spare gloves by the front door, otherwise by the time you get there and… oh, it was the string last time. I went to get some, stopped on the way to rinse a pot, and the string was still back in the shed. I’m usually better at sticking with things before lunch.”

I’d like help keeping hold of what I’m doing, or what I’m in the middle of saying. Sometimes the person I’m talking to looks puzzled, and then I realize I’ve gone off the point. It’s frustrating. I can’t really tell why some days are easier than others.

“When I’m tired I seem to find it harder to hang on to a thought long enough. Before lunch I usually manage better. It helps if I can put something in writing, like with the pencil my flatmate keeps beside the shopping list. Only when you’re talking to someone you can’t always stop in the middle and write… what was I going to say? That’s the part that gets frustrating, losing the point like that.”

“Before lunch is usually the time when I find it easier to stay with the point of a conversation. When I’m tired I can start to say something and lose track of where I meant to go with it. I find that frustrating.”

“I like being there with a practical job to get on with, although I do get sidetracked. That time I went for the string, I stopped along the way to rinse a pot and didn’t bring the string back. It’s frustrating to go there to help and then lose track of what I’m doing.”
Do you mean whether I already have a particular job in mind before I get there, or whether I pick one out once I’ve arrived?
Do you mean whether it helps me stick with what I’m doing if I’ve already decided on a job before I go there?

“Tiredness seems to make a difference because it feels harder to hold on to a thought when I’m tired. Before lunch is usually easier, though I still couldn’t really tell you why one day feels different from another.”
My flatmate keeps a pencil sitting next to the shopping list. I find that helpful because I can put the item straight onto the list, while I’ve still got it in mind, before I lose track of it.

“I find writing something down helps me keep track of it, like with the shopping list. It’s harder in conversation. Sometimes it’s the puzzled look on the other person’s face that makes me realize I’ve wandered away from the point. I get frustrated when I can’t hang on to what I was saying.”

I go to the pharmacy to pick up my medication. There was one collection I missed when the pharmacy changed its opening hours. I felt a little embarrassed about that, but I picked it up the following morning.

“I’d like us to talk again about ways of keeping track of what I’m doing, particularly keeping track of what I’m saying when I’m in a conversation. And maybe we could talk about what to say to my relative. They do count on me to help, and I’m not sure how I’d bring it up with them.”
